items.source_en:
Children of the Clone Wars

The war ended on paper long before it ended in people’s lives. Across the Republic, entire generations grew up amid evacuations, ration lines, and borrowed names. Some children learned to recognize starship silhouettes before letters. Others learned silence, understanding early which questions drew attention and which kept food on the table. By the time the fighting stopped, many of them were already working, already displaced, already accustomed to instability as a permanent condition.

As the galaxy reorganized itself, these children filled the gaps left behind. They became laborers, technicians, runners, clerks, and recruits. Some found structure in new institutions. Others drifted toward criminal networks that offered certainty where governments offered delays. The Clone Wars shaped them not through ideology, but through absence: absent parents, absent homes, absent futures promised and never delivered.

[This holobook is a sociological study of the generation raised during the Clone Wars, examining how mass conflict reshaped education, labor, loyalty, and identity, and how its youngest survivors quietly influenced the postwar galaxy.]
items.legacy_ko:
클론 전쟁의 아이들

전쟁은 사람들의 삶에서 끝나기 훨씬 전에 서류상으로 끝났습니다. 공화국 전역에서 전체 세대가 대피, 배급 줄, 빌린 이름들 속에서 자라났습니다. 어떤 아이들은 글자보다 우주선의 실루엣을 먼저 알아보는 법을 배웠습니다. 어떤 아이들은 침묵을 배웠고, 어떤 질문이 관심을 끌고 어떤 질문이 식탁에 음식을 올리는지 일찍이 이해했습니다. 전투가 멈췄을 때, 그들 중 다수는 이미 일하고 있었고, 이미 쫓겨났으며, 불안정을 영구적인 상태로 받아들이는 데 익숙해져 있었습니다.

locations.vanilla_source_en:
Charity in a Godless Universe

Amelia Sang

Part III:

When I was 19 years old, my church decided it was time to leave.

The announcement was filled with phrases like "fresh start" and "renewal". Apparently, our settlement had taken in too many non-believers. The congregation would pack up, and build a new colony on a distant world: a place without outsiders, where their faith could become the law.

"Cowards! You're running away!" I begged my family not to leave. "These people came here for our help. If we take their generators, how will the rest of the colony survive?"

To most of my community, these arguments made no difference. They could only see the outsiders as outsiders: non-believers, who were preventing them from living a pure life.

"These people have been coming here since you were a little girl." My father told me, one night, "They've had nearly twenty years to hear the word of god, but that's not what they want. We will leave them to their lives, and they should leave us to ours."

Word traveled quickly through the poor parts of the settlement. As the departure date neared, the other colonists became desperate. Protests were common outside of the church buildings, and outside of our Starport, where a large, arc-like ship was being constructed.

Finally, on departure day, dozens of colonists gathered at the entrance to the Starport. They blocked the church from entering - a hundred gaunt faces, against a hundred blue robes.

But the group was no match for the church's security forces. That team cleared a path, and the congregation boarded their arc. The crowd could only watch as the ship roared to life, and then vanished into the sky.

I stood in that crowd, watching as well. I could not bring myself to leave. Any faith which abandons the helpless was a faith I could not believe in. A loving god who inspired such cruelty must not be real. I would stay behind, for whatever came next.

items.source_en:
To anyone heading to Taleucema:

Don't.

The market district's a ghost town. Half the stalls are shuttered, the other half are Imperial "licensed vendors" selling marked-up goods at triple the price. 

Stormtroopers on every corner, checking chain codes, asking questions.

Javik's cantina? Gone. They arrested him for "unlicensed assembly." The Dusty Bantha's been empty for months now, windows boarded up.

Three checkpoints between the starport and the city center. They'll search your cargo, scan your ship, log your biometrics. If you're not human, they'll make you wait. If you're carrying anything "suspicious," you're detained. No trial, no explanation.

Saw them haul away the Twi'lek family that used to run the parts shop on Trader's Avenue. Their daughter was crying. Nobody helped. Nobody dared.

The city I knew, the one with music in the plazas and deals made over handshakes - that's dead. What's left is just uniforms and fear.

Stay away. Stay safe. Taleucema isn't worth it anymore.
items.legacy_ko:
탈레우세마로 향하는 모든 이들에게:

가지 마라.

시장 구역은 유령 도시가 되었다. 가게 절반은 문을 닫았고, 나머지는 제국 "허가 상인"들이 물건값을 세 배로 올려 팔고 있다.

모퉁이마다 스톰트루퍼들이 서서 체인 코드를 확인하고 질문을 던진다.

자빅의 칸티나는 사라졌다. "무허가 집회" 혐의로 그를 체포했다. 더스티 반타는 몇 달째 비어 있고 창문은 판자로 막혔다.

우주항과 도심 사이에 검문소만 세 개다. 화물을 뒤지고, 함선을 스캔하고, 생체 정보를 기록한다. 인간이 아니면 기다리게 만들 것이다. "의심스러운" 물건을 가지고 있으면 구금된다. 재판도, 설명도 없다.

트레이더스 애비뉴에서 부품 가게를 하던 트윌렉 가족을 끌고 가는 걸 봤다. 딸아이가 울고 있었다. 아무도 돕지 않았다. 아무도 감히 나서지 못했다.

내가 알던 도시, 광장에서 음악이 흐르고 악수로 거래가 이루어지던 그 도시는 죽었다. 남은 건 제복과 공포뿐이다.

멀리해라. 몸조심해라. 탈레우세마는 이제 그럴 가치가 없다.

From: Commander Natara
Subject: Safety of our Test Pilots
Date: 27 Telona, 7968 C.RC

Dr. Kang, 
MAST has indicated that the recent loss of test pilots is in no way a concern going forward for both Project ComSpike and Archangel.
